SUBJECT: HOUSING ASSISTANCE PAYMENTS PROGRAM – APPROVE
  WARRANT RUN AUGUST 15, 2021 – SEPTEMBER 1, 2021

Background:

The Housing Authority made payments during the period of August 15, 2021 through
September 1, 2021 for a grand total $616,139.74.

Fiscal Impact: N/A

Citizens Advised: N/A

Strategic Plan 2021 Implementation: N/A

Recommended Action:

Staff recommends the Housing Authority approve Check Nos. 67404 & 219328 - 219332
reported on August 15, 2021 for a total of $5,740.00; and Check Nos. 67405 – 67428 &
219333 – 219487 reported on September 1, 2021 for a total of $610,399.74.

Attachments:

1.  Check Summary Information Sheet
2.  Check Summary
   ATTACHMENT 1
  Housing Authority
  Check Summary Information Sheet

The warrants in the Housing Authority agenda report are for housing assistance payments
made under the Section 8 Housing Choice Voucher program. The payee has a choice of
receiving the housing assistance payment via direct deposit, which is an electronic fund
transfer made directly to the payee’s bank account, or by paper check.

In the check summary report, the direct deposits are listed first as direct deposits, and then
the checks follow. Each direct deposit and paper check represents payment for 1 to 20
tenants depending upon the number of Section 8 tenants the payee has.

The payee is the property owner or designated management company. The property owner
or manager may be a corporation, partnership, trust, or individual. The payee name is the
owner or manager’s legal business or individual name, which must match Internal Revenue
Service (IRS) records. Here are some common abbreviations used in business names:

LLC = Limited Liability Company

LP = Limited Partnership

DBA = “Doing Business As”

LTD = Limited

Checks made out to the City of Norwalk Housing Authority represent the Family Self
Sufficiency (FSS) escrow deposits. These checks are deposited into the Housing Authority’s
bank account where the funds earn interest and are kept in escrow until the FSS participant
successfully completes the program at which time they receive the balance of their account.

Norwalk Housing Investors, LP is the owner of Center Pointe Villas at 14100 San Antonio
and 11856 Orange. Payments are for Section 8 participants living in these buildings.

Payments to housing authorities, such as the Orange County Housing Authority and San
Bernardino County Housing, represent reimbursements for our participants who have
transferred to those jurisdictions under portability.

Please call Nida Watkins at ext. 5653 if you have any questions.

SUBJECT: RESOLUTION  NO.  NHA-166  -  DESTRUCTION  OF  OBSOLETE
  RECORDS

Background:

State law provides that certain City records, which are not required for legal or legislative
purposes, may be destroyed after two years. In addition, on February 17, 2009, City
Council adopted Resolution No. 09-05 establishing a records retention schedule for City
records. Attached is a list of obsolete records submitted by the Housing division that may
be destroyed pursuant to State law and the City’s adopted retention schedule. The
Authority Counsel has reviewed the list and approved destruction.

Fiscal Impact: N/A

Citizens Advised: N/A

Strategic Plan 2021 Implementation: N/A

Recommended Action:

Staff recommends the Housing Authority adopt Resolution No. NHA-166, A
RESOLUTION OF THE CITY OF NORWALK HOUSING AUTHORITY AUTHORIZING
THE DESTRUCTION OF CERTAIN RECORDS IN THE HOUSING DIVISION OF THE
COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DEPARTMENT.

Attachments:

1. Resolution No. NHA-166
2. Department Head Approval form with Authority to Destroy form.
   RESOLUTION NO. NHA-166

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY OF NORWALK HOUSING AUTHORITY
  AUTHORIZING THE DESTRUCTION OF CERTAIN RECORDS IN THE
  HOUSING DIVISION OF THE COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DEPARTMENT

  WHEREAS, Section 34090 of the Government Code provides for the destruction of
public records more than two years old with the consent of the Department Head and the
approval of the City Attorney and legislative body by resolution; and

  WHEREAS, the City Council adopted Resolution No. 09-05 on February 17, 2009
establishing a Records Retention Schedule, which identified City records and established
their retention.

  NOW, THEREFORE, THE CITY OF NORWALK HOUSING AUTHORITY DOES
HEREBY RESOLVE, DETERMINE AND ORDER AS FOLLOWS:

  Section 1.  In accordance with the City’s adopted Records Retention Schedule and
Government Code §34090, the following identified records are no longer required:

  •  Inactive Section 8 Case Files - June 30, 2017

  Section 2.  Pursuant to the approval of Authority Counsel, the Housing Authority
does hereby authorize the destruction of said records from the Housing Division.

  Section 3.  The Housing Authority hereby finds and determines that said
aforementioned records are more than two years old and/or no longer required nor are the
same required to be kept by statute or law.

  Section 4.  The Clerk is hereby directed to cause said records to be destroyed in
accordance with the terms and conditions of section 34090 of the government Code of the
State of California.

  Section 5.  That upon destruction of the identified records, the City Clerk’s
Department shall make a certification of destruction of such records and file the original of
same in the office of the City Clerk.

  APPROVED AND ADOPTED on this 21st day of September 2021.

  _______________________________
  JENNIFER PEREZ
  CHAIR

SUBJECT: CONTRACT AMENDMENT NO. 1 - AN INTERAGENCY AGREEMENT
  FOR PROJECT-BASED VOUCHERS AT THE BIRCH AND ELM
  HOUSING DEVELOPMENT

Background:

Homes for Life Foundation operates Birch Grove Homes (Birch) and Elm Street (Elm)
Homes located on the grounds of the Metropolitan State Hospital at 11400 Norwalk
Boulevard in Norwalk. The homes comprise 36 units, including two manager’s units,
providing permanent supportive housing for 34 chronically homeless, mentally ill
individuals.

The Los Angeles County Development Authority (LACDA) has been able to offer project-
based Section 8 vouchers to support the project since the original inter-agency agreement
was approved by the Norwalk Housing Authority (NHA) on May 16, 2017 for a period of
five years. Because the homes are located in the Norwalk NHA’s jurisdiction, LACDA is
only able to continue to provide funding to the homes if the NHA agrees to extend their
interagency agreement.

Under the amendment, LACDA would administer and fund the project-based vouchers at
Birch and Elm Homes. The NHA would have no financial or administrative obligations.
The term of the project-based assistance contract between LACDA and Homes for Life
expires on June 30, 2022 in accordance with the current interagency agreement between
LACDA and the NHA. This amendment would allow LACDA to extend the initial contract
term with Birch and Elm to a maximum of 15 years. Future renewals of the project-based
voucher contract between LACDA and Homes for Life Foundation would be subject to the
NHA approval and the extension of the interagency agreement.
 Housing Authority  September 21, 2021
Amendment No. 1 - Inter-Agency Agreement with LACDA  Page No. 2

On May 20, 2016, LACDA and NHA entered into an interagency agreement allowing
LACDA to administer Veterans Affairs Supportive Housing (VASH) vouchers in the City.
So far, everything has been going well with the VASH program in Norwalk. By extending
the interagency agreement for project-based vouchers at Birch Grove Homes and Elm
Street Homes, the NHA is assisting in the preservation of the homes and preventing
displacement of the residents, which could result in homelessness.

Fiscal Impact: N/A

Citizens Advised: N/A

Strategic Plan 2021 Implementation: N/A

Recommended Action:

Staff recommends the Housing Authority authorize the Executive Director to execute
Amendment No. 1 to the interagency agreement with the Los Angeles County
Development Authority for project-based vouchers at Birch Grove Homes and Elm Street
Homes.

Attachments:

Amendment No. 1 to the Interagency Agreement
   AMENDMENT NO.1 TO AGREEMENT
  BETWEEN
  THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY
  AND
  THE NORWALK HOUSING AUTHORITY
  RELATED TO THE PROJECT-BASED VOUCHER PROGRAM

This Amendment No.1 is made and entered into by and between the Los Angeles County
Development Authority, hereinafter referred to as “LACDA” and the Norwalk Housing
Authority, hereinafter referred to as “NHA” and shall commence on the date of execution
of the last signatory.

WHEREAS, the Housing Authority of the County of Los Angeles and the NHA entered
into an interagency agreement on June 14, 2017, to allow the housing authority to commit
project-based vouchers and enter into a Housing Assistance Payments (“HAP”) contract
with the Birch and Elm housing development located at 11401 Bloomfield Avenue in the
City of Norwalk; and

WHEREAS, on May 16, 2019, the Housing Authority dissolved as a separate legal entity
and merged with the Community Development Commission of the County of Los Angeles
("Commission"); and

WHEREAS, as a result of the merger, the Commission took title to the Housing Authority's
property, debts, demands, liabilities, and obligations; and

WHEREAS, following the merger, the Commission is now known as the Los Angeles
County Development Authority; and

WHEREAS, the Agreement expires on June 30, 2022 or upon termination of the HAP
Contract, whichever occurs earlier; and

WHEREAS, the parties wish to extend the Agreement by fifteen (15) years; and

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants herein set forth and the
mutual benefits to be derived therefrom, the parties agree as follows:

1. Section 3, TERM, has been deleted in its entirety and replaced by the following:

  This Agreement shall commence on June 14, 2017, and terminate on June 30,
  2037, or upon the termination of the HAP Contract, whichever occurs earlier.
 2. All other terms and conditions shall remain in full force and effect.
